subject: reasoning
question: 8 boys A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H are sitting in a row facing south (not necessarily in the same order). A and H are at extreme ends of the row. E and F are immediate neighbours of B. C is fourth to the left of B. F is to the immediate left of A. D is not the immediate neighbour of C. Who is sitting third to the right of E?
solution:
Given:

8 boys A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H are sitting in a row facing south.

A and H are at extreme ends of the row.

F is to the immediate left of A. Since they are facing south, A must be at the left end (from our perspective) so that F can be to his left.
